newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Haider claims legacy of socialist hero.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Haider claims legacy of socialist hero.

text.p: The leader of Austria's far-right, fresh from achieving big gains in European parliamentary elections, on Tuesday called his Freedom Party the voice of the people and heir to revered post-war chancellor Bruno Kreisky.

Joerg Haider, whose party won more than half the working class vote in Sunday's poll, said Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's Social Democrats had betrayed Kreisky's legacy by squeezing ordinary people while turning a blind eye to abuse of privilege.
"We have to make something of what Kreisky left behind. He chose the Social Democrats as his heirs but now it seems the Freedom Party has taken on most of the legacy," Haider told a news conference.
Austrians credit Kreisky, chancellor from 1970 to 1983, with creating an enviable welfare state and turning his party into the most successful social democratic movement in Europe.
The nationalist leader's remarks brought angry protests from Social Democratic headquarters.
"If Haider is looking for an historical role model, he should look back a bit further," party manager Brigitte Ederer said.

Kreisky's Social Democrats consistently scored more than 50 percent in the polls, now a distant memory for the party he left behind that scored its postwar low of 29.2 percent in Sunday's vote. Many ordinary Austrians used the vote to vent their anger at welfare cuts and rising unemployment.

"We have become the party of the workers. The Social Democrats were wiped out because they are arrogant and they have lost touch with ordinary people," said Haider, whose party scored 27.6 percent and trailed Vranitzky by just 60,000 votes.
"In his 10 years as chancellor, Vranitzky has reduced his party to a pile of rubble."
The perpetually-tanned populist pledged to fight for a revision of a two-year austerity budget, passed by parliament in March, and press Brussels to do more to ease unemployment.
The state had robbed small and medium business of incentives and raised the tax burden for ordinary workers while pensioners struggled to make ends meet, Haider said.
Vranitzky, chastened by Sunday's vote, called a meeting of party managers late on Monday to review the damage.

He later made vague promises to cut bureaucracy and put policy ideas across more clearly -- exactly the same pledges he made after a dismal vote for the Social Democrats in the October 1994 general election. The party did slightly better in a snap election last December.
Vranitzky resisted any change to the government line-up, defying calls from some regional party bosses who say he has lost touch with the grass roots.
Haider accused the ruling coalition and some European politicians of trying to demonise the Freedom Party, aided and abetted by the Austrian press.
European Parliament president Klaus Haensch acted like an "itinerant priest" before Sunday's poll, warning Austrians not to vote for the Freedom Party, Haider said.
"Austrians are more intelligent. They have learned to live with a press that is not always objective," he continued.
In 1986 Austria voted Kurt Waldheim to the presidency despite an international outcry over his attempts to suppress his war record in Adolf Hitler's Nazi army.
